Moreover f' has the sign of x on the real line, so positive f(0) is the global minimum and forces r=0. This simultaneously engineers the proper group obstruction and the desired signature instead of hoping either occurs randomly.

avoid: Relying on generic full-group families such as S8 or A8 when the objective is broad missing-group coverage.
Advancing elegant but single-mechanism hypotheses without evidence of complementary coverage.
Treating heterogeneous families as an unstructured mixture; E showed breadth, but S’s geometry-based consolidation was materially stronger.
Overweighting specialized block or Eisenstein lanes that perform well locally but have limited catalogue reach.
Inferring which hidden seeds or group-signature pairs produced the aggregate gains.
feedback.diagnosis: The generation strongly favored a unified, geometry-driven portfolio over single-family hypotheses. Winner S combined E’s broad proper-subgroup discovery, A’s block-system constructions, and D’s irreducible/discriminant control lane, producing the best aggregate result: 63 fresh missing pairs, 948 fresh pair hits, 60 fresh seed hits, and 4 discriminant improvements. E confirmed that heterogeneous structured families are effective, but its lower totals—35 fresh missing pairs and 643 pair hits—show that merely interleaving families was weaker than consolidating them by shared permutation geometry. A and D contributed useful specialized behavior but lacked sufficient breadth alone. B and C were pruned early because their generic S8/A8 targets were too narrow and offered little evidence of catalogue-wide discovery.
feedback.next_generation_direction: Start from S and run a geometry-lane ablation and rebalancing study: measure each explicit lane’s marginal contribution using only aggregate fresh-pair, fresh-seed, and discriminant metrics, remove redundant parameterizations, and redirect that budget toward underrepresented forced-action geometries. Keep D’s irreducible discriminant lane as a fixed control, while allocating most exploration to new structured families that force permutation actions not already represented by the size-2 blocks, size-4 blocks, nested binary actions, and dihedral fibers.

Compute those elementary symmetric values exactly from c and q using resultants or multiplication matrices in Q[t]/(c). Enumerate several deterministic strata: unrestricted cubic and q; square-discriminant cubic; q constant or linear with a norm-square congruence; and mildly sparse cubics. Monic-normalize over Q and apply the standard denominator scaling L^8 P(x/L) to obtain a monic integer octic. Reject zero constant terms, repeated-root discriminant zero, duplicate vectors, and cheap rational factors. Balance the strata and coefficient shells rather than allowing the generic stratum to consume the budget; use a separate injective fallback family only if retries are exhausted.

These subloci can reduce the generic signed-permutation group without inserting any known target polynomial.

For reciprocal x^4h(x+x^-1), count roots of h in (-infinity,-2] union [2,infinity) and construct h with the required interval occupancy. For Q(h), use monotonicity intervals or an exact Sturm check on the final octic. Apply exact Sturm counting to every accepted proposal, not only one lane; retry within the same signature cell on mismatch. Retain invariant-preserving p-adic congruences and cheap factor checks, exact deduplication, and an injective fallback for each signature quota.

Thus signature targeting can be added without guessing hidden groups or abandoning the successful geometry.

The resulting degree-8 polynomial has roots indexed by the eight nonzero 3-torsion points and generically realizes the transitive GL(2,3) action, with special mod-3 images producing proper transitive subgroups. This primitive eight-point geometry is unrelated to compositions, reciprocal pairs, iterated quadratics, or Dickson covers.

Derive the resultant formula once or evaluate it with a small exact polynomial determinant routine; normalize it to monic over Q and scale z by a deterministic common denominator so all coefficients are integral. Enumerate low-height nonsingular (A,B), several small nonzero k values, and modular strata that alter the rational 3-isogeny and determinant behavior without explicitly testing for catalogue groups. Reject discriminant-zero curves, degree drops, zero constant terms, repeated octics, and cheap rational factors. Reserve some budget for quadratic twists and short integral Weierstrass translations, which change arithmetic specializations without hard-coding examples. Finish with deterministic retries and an injective fallback.

hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different primitive algebraic construction based on the action of Galois on the eight nonzero vectors of E[3].

The nonzero 3-torsion representation supplies a natural primitive action with many arithmetic subgroup specializations. For a nonsingular real elliptic curve, complex conjugation fixes the nonzero real 3-torsion points, so this construction also has a strong, predictable r=2 bias—valuable because r=2 is comparatively rare in the incumbent and is missing in at least one entirely uncovered group.

hypotheses.implementation: Keep four explicit incumbent superfamilies: size-2 block covers, size-4 block covers, quadratic iterates, and Dickson/dihedral covers, plus a 15-20% low-height irreducible control. Merge reciprocal forms into the size-2 superfamily and assign disjoint parameter/support strata to avoid duplication. In the Dickson lane vary only the Dickson parameter, target constant, and integral affine conjugations that preserve the cover; remove arbitrary linear perturbations. In the iterate lane retain genuine third iterates minus a target. Use exact Sturm quotas across attainable signatures. Within each lane generate a small deterministic proposal batch and rank only within that same geometry by coefficient height, support novelty, repeated-prime polynomial-discriminant penalty, and cheap factor tests; never let a generic control proposal displace a structured quota. The control lane should alternate certified low-height Eisenstein and mod-p irreducible shapes and emphasize signatures associated with the listed large discriminant records. Guarantee exact uniqueness with seed-keyed counters and a provably injective fallback.
hypotheses.label: Invariant-faithful incumbent repair
hypotheses.mission: Exploit and improve the winning mechanisms by preserving their defining covers, removing redundant proposals, and adding efficient irreducibility and signature controls.
hypotheses.rationale: The critic explicitly recommends geometry-lane ablation and rebalancing while retaining the discriminant control. The current solver also generates four attempts and chooses a low-height proposal without measuring whether a deformation still belongs to its advertised cover. Faithful affine conjugation, target shifts, and branch-preserving changes give diversity without turning specialized lanes into generic S8 noise.

hypotheses.expected_result: Hits in product-action degree-8 groups poorly represented by the incumbent, with all four even signature regimes represented. Because low-discriminant factors are explicitly favored, the same run should also have a credible chance of improving difficult records such as covered r=0, r=4, and r=8 pairs even when a seed yields no new group.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Falsify if the construction yields no new missing pair and no field-discriminant improvement over the fresh evaluation, or if field intersections and reducibility push verified yield below 60%. Also reject the strategy if more than 75% of verified outputs occupy a single group despite balanced quartic strata, since that would show the proposed Cartesian portfolio is not genuinely exploring distinct actions.
hypotheses.hypothesis: If alpha has degree four, beta has degree two, and the fields are suitably disjoint, theta=alpha+beta has degree eight and its conjugates form a 4-by-2 Cartesian product. The polynomial Res_y(q(y),f(x-y)) therefore realizes constrained product subgroups rather than the full wreath groups favored by polynomial composition. Varying the quartic Galois geometry and the signatures of both factors should expose additional missing groups and signatures, while the discriminant behavior of a compositum of small-discriminant factors offers unusually strong secondary record potential.
hypotheses.implementation: Enumerate monic irreducible quartics f from balanced strata: generic low-height quartics; biquadratic/V4-oriented forms; cyclic-or-dihedral resolvent strata; reciprocal quartics; and p-adically certified sparse forms. Pair them with monic quadratics q having positive or negative discriminant and form F(x)=Res_y(q(y),f(x-y)); for a quadratic q this resultant can be implemented directly as a norm in Q[y]/(q), avoiding a general symbolic package. Add a few small multipliers theta=alpha+k beta to prevent systematic collisions. Prefer disjointness using deterministic modular factorization fingerprints and reject degree drops, zero constants, repeated vectors, or cheap rational factors. Schedule cells by quartic stratum, factor signatures, k, and expanding height shell using a low-discrepancy round robin. For each cell compare several candidates only by factor discriminants, final polynomial-discriminant bit length, height, and support novelty; preserve a fixed exploration quota so discriminant scoring cannot consume the whole budget. Use an injective fallback outside the compositum lanes only after bounded retries.
hypotheses.label: Low-discriminant compositum frontier
hypotheses.mission: Provide a complementary exploration portfolio based on Cartesian-product actions of independently generated quadratic and quartic fields, with an explicit low-discriminant frontier.
hypotheses.rationale: This construction has the same degree decomposition as some incumbent lanes but a different Galois constraint: both coordinates move globally and independently, rather than allowing separate fiber permutations. It supplies a useful exploration portfolio through several quartic factor families and gives signatures multiplicatively—0,2,4, or 8—without expensive blind Sturm rejection. Small quadratic and quartic fields also provide a principled path toward lowering difficult absolute field discriminants.

details.thesis: Preserve the incumbent’s geometry-first principle, but replace redundant or geometry-destroying parameterizations with five orthogonal searches: signed-cube actions for absent groups, explicit archimedean steering for missing signatures, elliptic 3-torsion for a new primitive action, faithful repairs of proven incumbent covers, and low-discriminant composita as a complementary product-action portfolio. Every implementation must use seed-keyed counter enumeration, exact-vector deduplication, deterministic retries, and an injective monic fallback so it returns exactly the requested number of unique valid vectors.

avoid: Treating screen or preliminary scores as sufficient evidence when seed-consistency validation fails, as in D.
Expanding S with additional families before measuring overlap and marginal yield within its two existing branches.
Returning to narrow single-geometry proposals such as A, C, or E without a demonstrated complementary lane.
Assuming that signature targeting alone will improve catalogue coverage without benchmark evidence, as B did not reach that stage.
Claiming discriminant progress from blank fields or from the inconsistent prior summary; the reported benchmarked candidates show zero improvements where values are present.
Inferring the identities of hidden seeds, groups, or group–signature pairs from aggregate counts.
feedback.diagnosis: S won because it converted the strongest ideas from A and E into one coherent orbit-polynomial portfolio. It produced 5 fresh missing pairs, 166 fresh pair hits, and all 60 fresh seed hits—clearly exceeding A’s 2/98/58 and E’s 2/18/15. The complementary geometries mattered: the signed-cube branch supplied stronger discovery density, while the quadratic–quartic branch supplied broader group coverage and better verification. A showed that signed-cube geometry is productive but insufficient alone; E’s Cartesian composita added useful but weaker complementary reach. D’s portfolio-repair idea earned strong preliminary scores but failed seed consistency and ultimately delivered only 2 fresh pairs from 2 seeds, so its apparent promise did not translate into robust performance. B’s signature-chamber proposal and C’s GL(2,3) construction were pruned before benchmark evidence established broad value. No reported finalist produced a discriminant improvement, so the generation improved catalogue coverage rather than low-discriminant records. The previous feedback’s larger aggregate counts and claimed discriminant gains are inconsistent with the supplied generation results and should not guide the next iteration.
feedback.next_generation_direction: Start from S and run a fixed-budget ablation/rebalancing experiment over its two branches. Partition each branch into explicit parameter sublanes, record only aggregate verification rate, fresh-pair hits, fresh missing-pair count, and discriminant improvements, then remove sublanes whose marginal discoveries are redundant. Reallocate most recovered budget to new forced-action geometries outside signed cubes and 4×2 Cartesian products, while reserving a small fixed quota for an independently verified discriminant-focused control. Require every proposed addition to beat the retained S sublanes on marginal missing-pair yield across repeated seed batches before it enters the portfolio.
what_worked: Combining two explicitly complementary permutation geometries in a shared orbit-polynomial framework.
Prioritizing signed-cube orbits for discovery: the reported branch comparison favored them with 3 new pairs and 102 fresh-pair hits.
Retaining quadratic–quartic Cartesian orbits for their higher verification rate and wider group coverage.
Preserving broad seed reach: S achieved fresh hits on all 60 seeds while improving missing-pair discovery.
Using forced-action structure to target proper transitive subgroups instead of relying on generic full-group behavior.

hypotheses.expected_result: This should have lower raw verification than the incumbent but materially greater group novelty, with success defined by at least one entirely missing group rather than many additional hits in known groups. The asymmetric lane should supply the broadest tree group, while coefficient-deletion and square-class lanes should expose proper transitive subgroups and multiple signatures.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Across repeated fresh-seed batches, compare each tower lane against equal-size retained incumbent lanes. Falsify the hypothesis if no entirely missing group appears, if all verified outputs collapse to already covered groups, or if apparent discoveries occur in only one seed batch. Remove any sublane whose marginal missing-pair yield is zero or wholly redundant with another tower lane.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Octics obtained from asymmetric three-stage quadratic towers Q ⊂ Q(u) ⊂ Q(u,v) ⊂ Q(u,v,x) realize subgroups of the depth-three binary-tree automorphism group. Generic, rank-deficient, and partially symmetric tower parameters should reach several small imprimitive transitive groups that the incumbent's cube-translation and Cartesian actions systematically miss, including candidates among the entirely uncovered low-index groups.
hypotheses.implementation: Enumerate bounded deterministic integer tuples (p,a,b,c,d,e,f) from seed, lane, shell, and counter. Set u^2=p, v^2=a+bu, and x^2=c+du+ev+fuv. Compute the octic exactly as the successive norm of x^2-(c+du+ev+fuv): write it as A+Bv, reduce A^2-(a+bu)B^2 modulo u^2=p to C+Du, then return C^2-pD^2. Use distinct lanes for fully asymmetric tuples, f=0, e=0, d=0, and controlled square-class coincidences; do not permit degeneracies that visibly split a tower level. Stratify accepted candidates by exact Sturm root count and finite-field factor-degree sketches, with quotas favoring 0, 4, and 8 real roots but retaining 2 and 6. Apply the rational-factor subset-sum sieve rather than requiring an irreducible reduction, since some relevant transitive 2-groups contain no 8-cycle. Canonicalize under x↦-x, reject zero constants and duplicates, and fill any exhausted cells with a counter-derived 2-Eisenstein octic so the output is exactly budget unique monic vectors.
hypotheses.label: Asymmetric quadratic towers
hypotheses.mission: Attack entirely missing groups using a transitive action absent from the signed-cube and 4-by-2 Cartesian incumbent.
hypotheses.rationale: The incumbent covered only seven groups despite excellent seed reach, so further sampling inside its two actions is unlikely to expose all missing groups. A nested tower has a hierarchical block system—four sibling pairs inside two blocks of four—rather than the cube's affine translations or a fixed 4-by-2 product. Varying which tower coefficients vanish or share square classes naturally traverses different transitive subgroups without encoding catalogue identities.

hypotheses.expected_result: The paired chamber shifts should reproduce some already seen groups at new real-root counts and thereby fill missing signatures without requiring discovery of a new group. A useful candidate should show higher missing-signature yield per verified polynomial than blind incumbent signature scheduling, not merely a different distribution of r.
hypotheses.falsification_test: For every cover/base lane, compare targeted thresholds with matched untargeted thresholds across multiple fresh seeds. Falsify if signature quotas are achieved but missing-pair yield does not increase, if group identities change so completely that the chamber intervention is not isolating signature, or if gains fail seed consistency. Do not promote the method on screen score alone.
hypotheses.hypothesis: For imprimitive groups already observed at only some signatures, the missing signatures are often rare archimedean chambers rather than absent algebraic groups. Quartic bases placed in certified root intervals and lifted through quadratic composition or reciprocal covers can move the same broad finite permutation mechanisms into r=0,2,4,6,8 chambers, especially the numerous missing r=4 and r=8 pairs.
hypotheses.implementation: Construct monic irreducible quartics as g(y)=∏_{i=1}^4(y-m_i)+δ using separated deterministic integers m_i and small nonzero δ chosen by exact sign checks to retain prescribed roots in disjoint rational intervals; include two-real-root and no-real-root quartic templates as separate lanes. Lift them in two ways. First form g((x-h)^2-t), where a real base root contributes two real roots exactly when it exceeds -t. Second form x^4 g(x+x^{-1}), where each real base root outside [-2,2] contributes two real roots. Verify the resulting octic's actual signature with exact Sturm computation rather than trusting the template. Pair each base with several threshold choices crossing one chamber wall at a time, but emit at most one candidate per finite-field factor-pattern bucket before revisiting it. Use deterministic modular subset-sum screening, canonical deduplication, nonzero-constant checks, and counter-derived Eisenstein fallbacks to satisfy the exact-budget contract.
hypotheses.label: Certified cover chambers
hypotheses.mission: Fill missing signatures in partially covered groups while preserving explicit degree-two cover geometry.
hypotheses.rationale: The previous signature proposal had a strong screen score but was pruned before benchmark evidence, so signature targeting remains unproved. This version makes the intervention testable: base-polynomial construction, cover type, and chamber are crossed systematically, and each targeted cell has an untargeted matched control. The two covers have explicit root-count rules and inequivalent block actions, preventing the experiment from being merely a coefficient bias.

hypotheses.expected_result: The generic lane should concentrate in one GL(2,3)-type transitive group, while reducible-division-polynomial and exceptional-image lanes may reach proper transitive subgroups. Even one missing pair would validate this independent arithmetic geometry; multiple signatures would justify a small permanent portfolio allocation.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Falsify if the determinant routinely has degree below eight, verification is prohibitively low, or all verified candidates land in groups already supplied more efficiently by the incumbent. Require discoveries on more than one fresh seed and audit that exceptional lanes remain transitive rather than merely producing reducible torsion orbits.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Primitive-element polynomials for the eight nonzero points of an elliptic curve's 3-torsion realize the transitive GL(2,3) action and selected proper mod-3 image subgroups. This four-block-of-two geometry is arithmetic rather than compositional and should access group/signature pairs poorly represented by radical cubes and Cartesian composita.
hypotheses.implementation: Enumerate nonsingular curves E:y^2=x^3+3ax+B with deterministic small integers a,B and 4(3a)^3+27B^2 nonzero. Their normalized 3-division polynomial is D(T)=T^4+6aT^2+4BT-3a^2. For deterministic nonzero k, take z=y+kx. In the rank-four algebra Z[T]/(D), build the 4-by-4 multiplication matrix of H_z(T)=(z-kT)^2-(T^3+3aT+B); its determinant is a monic integral degree-eight polynomial whose roots correspond to the eight nonzero 3-torsion points. Use exact polynomial arithmetic only. Cross curve lanes defined by small discriminant, rational 3-isogeny indicators detectable from factorization of D, and generic D, while using finite-field factor sketches solely for diversity. Reject singular curves, degree drops, zero constants, duplicates, and candidates failing the rational-factor subset-sum sieve. Stratify by exact Sturm signature and use deterministic Eisenstein fallbacks if the bounded construction pool is exhausted.
hypotheses.label: Elliptic 3-torsion octics
hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different arithmetic construction based on a linear action on nonzero 3-torsion points.
hypotheses.rationale: The earlier GL(2,3) proposal was pruned before establishing benchmark value, but it supplied a genuinely independent permutation representation. Choosing curves with A divisible by 3 makes the normalized 3-division polynomial monic integral, removing the earlier construction's likely denominator and normalization burden. Varying the curve and primitive element can explore both generic and exceptional mod-3 images without encoding any catalogue polynomial.

hypotheses.expected_result: The constrained lane should trade some verification rate for access to lower-order transitive cube groups and should produce group identities absent from matched generic cubes. Because the relation is exact, any gain should remain stable across seeds; low-height square-norm specializations may also incidentally improve discriminants, though that is not the acceptance criterion.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Run equal treatment/control quotas over repeated fresh seeds. Falsify if the norm-square lane has no higher marginal missing-pair yield, if it mostly becomes reducible, or if its verified group/signature distribution is statistically indistinguishable from the perturbed controls. Retain only the base-cubic sublane that contributes nonredundant discoveries.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The incumbent signed-cube lane usually has three independent radical square classes. Forcing the product of its three radicands to be a rational square reduces the Kummer rank and replaces the generic C2^3 sign kernel by an even-parity C2^2 kernel. The resulting proper transitive subgroups should complement, rather than duplicate, the incumbent's high-yield generic cubes.
hypotheses.implementation: Choose deterministic integers a,b,m,s and orientation ε in {−1,1}. Define the monic cubic c(T)=T^3+aT^2+bT+c0 with c0=εs^2-m^3-am^2-bm, so c(m)=εs^2. For each root α_i take d_i=ε(m-α_i); then ∏d_i=s^2 exactly. Compute the elementary symmetric functions e1,e2,e3 of the d_i in the cubic quotient algebra and emit the signed-sum orbit polynomial ∏_{δ_i=±1}(x-Σδ_i√d_i), using the existing exact even-octic formula; e3 must equal s^2 as an internal invariant check. Use matched control lanes with the same a,b,m and a one-unit perturbation of c0 that destroys the square relation. Separate generic S3-base cubics from bounded scans of cyclic cubic bases, and stratify both treatment and control by Sturm signature and finite-field pattern. Enforce cubic irreducibility, octic subset-sum screening, canonical uniqueness, nonzero constant, and exact-budget deterministic fallback.
hypotheses.label: Square-class collapsed cubes
hypotheses.mission: Improve the strongest incumbent mechanism by forcing a new Kummer relation instead of resampling its generic parameter space.
hypotheses.rationale: Signed cubes produced the best discovery density in the accepted solver, but its current q(α) sampling almost never enforces an exact square-class relation. This is a mathematically sharp ablation: matched generic and norm-square cubes share the same base-cubic and signature machinery, so any new-group gain can be attributed to kernel collapse. It directly follows the critic's request to measure marginal sublane yield before expanding the portfolio.

hypotheses.expected_result: The structured 85–90% should improve group and missing-pair breadth, while the isolated low-height control may occasionally lower difficult S8 or other already-solved records. Success requires discoveries from at least two grammars; a single dominant grammar should be split out and rebenchmarked rather than hidden inside the portfolio average.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Ablate novelty selection against equal-size round-robin sampling from the identical pool over repeated seeds. Falsify if modular-sketch diversity does not increase actual missing-pair yield, if discoveries come from only one unstable seed or grammar, or if the discriminant control reports no evaluator-confirmed field-discriminant improvements and reduces primary discovery enough to matter. Count only explicit benchmarked improvements, never missing summary fields.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A deterministic oversized pool selected for rarity of combined real-signature and finite-field factorization sketches will cover more transitive-group mechanisms than fixed quotas alone. Applying this novelty selection to reciprocal, Dickson, Kummer-sparse, and low-height Eisenstein grammars should recover the breadth once seen from the heterogeneous portfolio while avoiding redundant regions already dominated by cubes and Cartesian composita.
hypotheses.implementation: Generate a deterministic pool of roughly six times budget from four grammars that exclude signed cubes and quadratic-quartic Cartesian sums: reciprocal lifts x^4q(x+x^{-1}); Dickson combinations D8(x,a)+uD4(x,a)+vD2(x,a)+w using D0=2, D1=x, and Dn=xD_{n-1}-aD_{n-2}; sparse Kummer-style octics x^8+ux^j+vx^k+w with several fixed exponent shapes; and trace-normalized 2-Eisenstein octics of small height. Compute exact Sturm signature and squarefree factor-degree partitions at a fixed public list of small primes. Greedily select candidates by least-filled (grammar,signature,pattern) cells, then farthest Hamming distance between pattern sketches, with deterministic coefficient height as the final tie-breaker. Reserve 10–15% of output for the Eisenstein lane ranked by exact polynomial discriminant and height as a proxy only; actual number-field discriminant improvements must come from evaluation. Canonicalize, reject zero constants and duplicates, and continue counter enumeration until exactly budget unique monic octics are selected.
hypotheses.label: Frobenius-novelty portfolio
hypotheses.mission: Provide complementary exploration across unrelated polynomial grammars, with a small independently measured low-discriminant control.
hypotheses.rationale: The first-generation heterogeneous portfolio found many missing pairs and some reported discriminant improvements, whereas the current incumbent achieves broad seed reach but only seven groups. Cheap Frobenius cycle sketches cannot identify a hidden group, but they can suppress repeated local behavior. The discriminant lane is explicitly isolated so blank or inconsistent summaries cannot be mistaken for a real field-discriminant improvement.

details.thesis: Preserve the incumbent lesson that forced permutation structure beats generic coefficient sampling, but expand beyond its two geometries. The five candidates separately test hierarchical quadratic towers, certified signature chambers, elliptic 3-torsion actions, a deliberately rank-collapsed signed-cube mechanism, and modular-novelty portfolio selection. Missing-pair yield is the primary acceptance statistic; discriminant claims count only when the evaluator reports an actual smaller number-field discriminant.

hypotheses.expected_result: The output should have high irreducibility and should contribute transitive groups not seen from the incumbent geometries. Success means at least one wholly missing group on repeated fresh-seed batches, with discoveries distributed across more than one tower sublane rather than arising from a single exceptional seed.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Run at least three disjoint fresh-seed batches and compare against an equal-budget incumbent control. Reject the hypothesis if it produces no entirely missing group, if more than half its verified outputs collapse into incumbent-covered groups, or if any apparent discovery disappears under seed-consistency validation.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Primitive elements in genuinely nested three-step quadratic towers have an eight-point binary-tree action distinct from both signed-cube translations and quadratic–quartic Cartesian products. Generic towers and norm-constrained specializations should realize several small imprimitive transitive groups that broad coefficient searches systematically miss, making this a plausible route into entirely absent groups.
hypotheses.implementation: Represent each quadratic tower as an exact rank-8 integral algebra with basis 1,s1,s2,s1s2,s3,s1s3,s2s3,s1s2s3. Deterministically enumerate small nonsquare d and coefficients for the second and third radicands from the public seed. Form a primitive element theta=c1*s1+c2*s2+c3*s3+c12*s1*s2 using small nonzero coefficients, and compute det(xI-M_theta) by fraction-free elimination. Divide the budget among generic towers, towers where the first relative norm is parametrically a square, towers with conjugate-linked third radicands, and palindromic tower involutions; these are distinct action sublanes rather than height tweaks. Reject collapsed-degree cases, zero constants, repeated canonical vectors, and candidates whose good-prime subset-sum sieve still permits a rational factor. Expand the deterministic parameter shell until exactly budget vectors are returned; use no universal fallback polynomial.
hypotheses.label: Nested quadratic-tower norms
hypotheses.mission: Attack entirely missing transitive groups through non-Cartesian towers of quadratic extensions.
hypotheses.rationale: Many wholly missing groups are likely inaccessible to the incumbent because its cube branch begins with three parallel square roots over a cubic algebra, while its Cartesian branch has only one two-block layer. A non-Galois chain K1=Q(sqrt(d)), K2=K1(sqrt(u+v sqrt(d))), K3=K2(sqrt(w)) instead forces a nested block chain. Parametric conditions on successive norms create meaningful subgroup changes without identifying any catalogue group or embedding a known answer.

hypotheses.expected_result: Relative to the incumbent, the verified group distribution should remain recognizable while fresh hits shift toward missing signatures. The main expected gains are totally real completions and four-real-root completions in partially covered imprimitive groups, with occasional r=2 or r=6 discoveries.
hypotheses.falsification_test: On repeated equal-budget seed batches, require a higher number of fresh missing signatures than the unconditioned incumbent while retaining at least 80% of its verified-group breadth. Reject if the method merely redistributes root counts within already-solved pairs, materially lowers irreducibility, or fails seed consistency.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The incumbent reaches useful groups but wastes many outputs in already-covered real-root chambers. Conditioning its algebraic parameters before construction, then certifying the resulting root count exactly, should move substantial mass to r=4 and r=8—and smaller reserved quotas to r=2 and r=6—without sacrificing the forced group actions responsible for its coverage.
hypotheses.implementation: Retain only invariant-preserving signed-cube and quadratic–quartic constructions. For Cartesian sums, generate quartics in certified 0-, 2-, and 4-real-root chambers and choose the quadratic discriminant so the resultant has the scheduled root count. For signed cubes, compute the quartic R with P(x)=R(x^2), use a Sturm sequence on (0,infinity), and accept only the scheduled signature. Use a deterministic global signature schedule weighted toward 8 and 4, with fixed small quotas for 2 and 6 and a control quota for 0; do not encode any group-to-signature mapping. Oversample each cell, then choose candidates by least-used family/signature/Frobenius-factorization bucket and coefficient height. Transfer an exhausted cell to the least-filled compatible chamber, never to a seed-independent fallback, until exactly budget unique monic vectors are obtained.
hypotheses.label: Signature-conditioned orbit chambers
hypotheses.mission: Fill missing signatures in groups that the productive incumbent geometries already reach.
hypotheses.rationale: The previous signature proposal was pruned before benchmark evidence, so signature targeting itself was not disproved. Its weakness was being detached from demonstrated group-producing mechanisms. In the Cartesian branch, the quadratic discriminant and quartic root count determine the octic root count; in the cube branch, the octic is R(x^2), so its real-root count is twice the number of positive roots of R. These give exact, inexpensive chambers inside known productive families.

hypotheses.expected_result: This should add primitive or otherwise non-incumbent groups, including a realistic chance of reaching one or more entirely missing groups. Even when no new group appears, its Frobenius fingerprints should be markedly different from those of signed cubes and Cartesian sums.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject if either lane contributes no verified octics at useful density, if the combined output discovers no group outside the incumbent's group set over three fresh-seed batches, or if all fresh discoveries come from only one seed. Also reject if integrality normalization silently changes roots or produces nonmonic vectors.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Degree-eight orbit polynomials obtained from index-eight subgroup invariants can reach primitive transitive actions absent from binary cubes, block products, reciprocal lifts, and ordinary compositions. Two algebraically independent realizations—an S4/C3 quartic resolvent and the action on the eight nonzero 3-torsion points of an elliptic curve—should prevent this from becoming another narrow single-geometry bet.
hypotheses.implementation: For the quartic lane, generate irreducible monic quartics and algorithmically construct the eight conjugates of an invariant such as r1^2*r2+r2^2*r3+r3^2*r1 under S4 modulo its C3 stabilizer. Multiply the orbit factors and reduce symmetric expressions to the elementary symmetric coefficients of the input quartic; cache only the universal symbolic reduction, never instantiated catalogue polynomials. For the elliptic lane, enumerate curves y^2=x^3+3a*x+b, use the monic integral polynomial psi3/3=x^4+6a*x^2+4b*x-3a^2, and eliminate x from it and (z-kx)^2-(x^3+3a*x+b). Vary small nonzero k and a second integral linear observable so degeneracies do not dominate. Primitive-normalize only expressions already monic integral; reject every nonmonic, repeated, inseparable, zero-constant, or sieve-inconclusive result. Allocate both lanes fixed nontrivial quotas and enlarge parameter shells deterministically to return exactly budget unique vectors.
hypotheses.label: Index-eight invariant resolvents
hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different primitive/coset-action construction.
hypotheses.rationale: Both lanes produce eight conjugates because of a genuine group orbit, not because degrees two and four were multiplied. The quartic lane exposes a coset action through a cyclic-order-three invariant of four roots. The elliptic lane exposes the natural eight-point linear action on nonzero vectors over F3. Their unrelated degeneracy loci and ramification patterns make overlapping failures unlikely, while neither requires knowledge of catalogue labels.

hypotheses.expected_result: The verified fraction should rise materially above 0.754, duplicate and reducible statuses should fall, and fresh-seed reach should remain near complete. The stronger effective budget should match or exceed the incumbent's five missing pairs and may naturally lower records through the height tie-breaker.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Benchmark against the unchanged incumbent on identical repeated seed sets. Reject if verified fraction does not exceed 0.85, if fresh missing-pair count falls below the control, or if the apparent preliminary advantage again collapses under seed-consistency validation. Report discriminant improvements only when the evaluator supplies a concrete smaller field discriminant.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The accepted solver leaves measurable value on the table through redundant quartic parameterizations, shallow bounded retries, weak rational-factor screening, and seed-independent fallback outputs. A larger invariant-preserving candidate pool followed by balanced novelty selection should preserve the cube branch's discovery density, the Cartesian branch's breadth, and substantially improve usable candidates per slot.
hypotheses.implementation: Generate an internal pool of at least five times budget. Keep the four genuinely different signed-cube sublanes, but separate their cubic-Galois and q-shape cases in the balancing key. In the Cartesian branch retain generic, even, reciprocal, and Eisenstein quartics while removing the coefficient-reversal duplicate as an independent quota. Reweight modestly toward signed cubes based on their measured discovery advantage, but preserve at least one third of selected outputs for Cartesian breadth. Replace the four-prime permissive sieve with an incremental good-prime factor-degree intersection over more small primes, accepting only when every possible rational factor degree 1 through 4 is excluded. Select greedily by least-used family/sublane/signature/Frobenius fingerprint, then coefficient height. Continue deterministic shell expansion rather than emitting fallbacks, and canonicalize under x to -x before insertion so every call returns exactly budget unique vectors.
hypotheses.label: Ablated incumbent selector
hypotheses.mission: Exploit the accepted mechanisms while removing redundancy, reducibility, and fallback-induced overlap.
hypotheses.rationale: The accepted generation produced five missing pairs and hit all fresh seeds, so its core geometry is a strong control. Its frozen run nevertheless contained 288 reducibles and 204 duplicate candidates, while the source includes two nearly interchangeable generic quartic lanes and deterministic fallback polynomials unrelated to the seed. Repairing those mechanisms is more consequential than changing a few coefficient ranges.

hypotheses.expected_result: The structural majority should add pair discoveries not duplicated by the incumbent, while the protected control can improve one of the conspicuously large existing discriminants without overwhelming the primary search. Selected outputs should span more signatures, local cycle patterns, and ramification profiles than a simple family round-robin.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Compare the maximin selector with an equal-pool round-robin ablation over at least three fresh-seed batches. Reject if it does not improve marginal missing-pair yield, if one family supplies nearly all selected fingerprints or discoveries, or if the discriminant lane consumes slots without a verified field-discriminant improvement. Polynomial-discriminant proxies alone do not count as record gains.
hypotheses.hypothesis: A portfolio selected by maximin diversity of exact local factorization and ramification fingerprints will cover more useful territory than round-robin family enumeration. Combining non-incumbent reciprocal trace lifts, non-autonomous quadratic preimage trees, square-discriminant critical-value octics, and a small Eisenstein low-height control should discover complementary proper groups while giving difficult discriminant records a genuine opportunity to improve.
hypotheses.implementation: Deterministically oversample four lanes: reciprocal trace polynomials x^4*g(x+x^-1) with invariant-preserving deformations; non-autonomous compositions q1(q2(q3(x)))-t with independent centered monic quadratics and correlated sublanes; monic octics obtained by integrating f'(x)=8x*q(x)^2 under explicit divisibility conditions and choosing the integration constant to force square discriminant; and low-height trace-normalized Eisenstein octics. Give the first three lanes at least 80% of the budget and reserve the remainder for the discriminant control. For every valid candidate compute exact signature, polynomial discriminant, valuations at small primes, and good-prime factor-degree partitions. Greedily select the candidate maximizing distance from already selected fingerprints, with missing signature rarity as the first tie-breaker and log absolute polynomial discriminant plus coefficient height as later tie-breakers. Maintain fixed minimum quotas per structural lane, canonical uniqueness, and deterministic shell expansion until exactly budget outputs exist.
hypotheses.label: Local-global diversity portfolio
hypotheses.mission: Explore complementary structural families with local novelty selection and a protected low-discriminant lane.
hypotheses.rationale: Earlier broad portfolios worked, but simply adding more families now risks redundant outputs. Local fingerprints provide a catalogue-free way to measure overlap before spending output slots. The structural lanes force different involutions, tree stabilizers, or discriminant parity, while the control lane supplies guaranteed irreducibility and small-height candidates for already-solved generic pairs.

details.thesis: Use the accepted orbit engine only as a measured control, and spend most experimental diversity on forced actions absent from its signed-cube and 4-by-2 Cartesian branches. Every lane must deterministically oversample, enforce monicity, nonzero constant term and canonical uniqueness, then select by exact signature and finite-prime fingerprints. Judge additions by repeated-seed marginal missing-pair yield; verification rate and discriminant gains are secondary tie-breakers, never substitutes for new pairs.

avoid: Treating D or S as promising benchmark winners when both implementations timed out before producing measurements.
Repeating the previous feedback's incorrect claim that S won or that E had only narrow, weak reach.
Scaling A into a primary strategy without improving its verification rate and marginal yield per computational slot.
Interpreting C's pruning as proof that its constructions fail; there is simply no benchmark evidence yet.
Returning to signature targeting alone after B produced zero fresh pairs, pair hits, and seed hits.
Inferring hidden seed identities or hidden group-signature identities from aggregate results.
feedback.diagnosis: E clearly won this generation by combining robust seed-wide coverage with genuine novelty: 6 fresh missing pairs, 67 fresh pair hits across all 60 fresh seeds, and the only reported discriminant improvement. Its maximin selection over exact local factorization and ramification fingerprints appears to have turned several complementary polynomial families into a reliable portfolio rather than a narrow construction. A validated nested quadratic towers as a real but sparse secondary source: it found 2 fresh missing pairs and 9 fresh pair hits on 9 seeds, yet its lower verification/yield and lack of discriminant progress kept it behind E. B's signature-conditioning idea produced no measured gain. C was pruned before benchmark evidence, so its primitive-action constructions remain unvalidated rather than disproved. D and S failed through solver timeouts; their hypotheses therefore provide no performance evidence. The supplied results also supersede the inconsistent previous summary, which incorrectly described S as the winner and misreported branch totals.
feedback.next_generation_direction: Use E as the fixed backbone and run a budget-controlled family ablation. Measure each of E's four lanes separately by verification rate, fresh missing pairs, fresh pair hits, seed reach, discriminant improvements, and runtime; then retain the smallest mixture that preserves most of E's 6/67/60 performance. Allocate the recovered budget to a tightly capped nested-tower lane derived from A, but admit it to the permanent portfolio only if repeated batches show positive marginal missing-pair yield after deduplication against E. Keep the same fingerprint-based selector across all lanes and enforce per-lane time limits so the D/S timeout failure cannot recur.
what_worked: E's diversity-driven portfolio achieved discoveries on all 60 fresh seeds instead of relying on rare favorable seeds.
Combining reciprocal trace lifts, non-autonomous quadratic preimage trees, square-discriminant critical-value octics, and a small Eisenstein control produced complementary coverage.
Selecting candidates by exact local factorization and ramification fingerprints yielded 67 fresh pair hits and 6 previously missing pairs.
E produced the generation's sole explicitly reported discriminant improvement, showing that discovery and record-oriented search can coexist.
A's genuinely nested quadratic towers found 2 missing pairs, confirming that their forced eight-point actions offer some complementary value despite sparse yield.

hypotheses.expected_result: A modest verified fraction but positive marginal discovery yield, with at least one pair from an entirely missing group being the key success criterion. Hits should be concentrated in groups poorly represented by the incumbent’s independent-sign and composition geometries.
hypotheses.falsification_test: On matched fresh seeds, compare the constrained sublanes with the unconstrained tower control after cross-deduplication. Reject the hypothesis if the complete implementation finds no entirely missing group or pair, or if every constrained sublane has zero marginal fresh-pair yield while materially lowering verification throughput.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The entirely missing groups include actions that broad reciprocal, Cartesian, and preimage-tree families rarely realize because those families impose either independent sign changes or repeated cover geometry. Primitive elements of genuinely nested towers Q⊂Q(u)⊂Q(u,v)⊂Q(u,v,w), with u²=a, v²=b0+b1u, and w²=c0+c1u+c2v+c3uv, instead carry the full binary-tree action. Alternating generic parameters with norm-square and conjugate-pair constraints should sample several distinct transitive subgroups of that action and can reach whole groups absent from the current catalogue coverage.
hypotheses.implementation: Use the integral basis [1,u,v,uv,w,uw,vw,uvw]. For each deterministic parameter tuple, construct the 8-by-8 integer multiplication matrix of theta=w+lambda*v+mu*u+nu*uv and return its characteristic polynomial in ascending coefficient order. Populate four equal sublanes: unconstrained towers; b0²-a*b1² forced to a nonzero square; that norm forced to a times a square; and final radicands paired with their K1 conjugates through simple norm or trace relations. Enumerate small shells first, then geometrically larger shells, with all signs and sublane choices obtained from a public seed mixer. Reject zero radicands, repeated tower levels, zero discriminants, duplicate canonical polynomials, and candidates whose good-prime factor patterns remain compatible with a rational factor. Use root count and factorization/ramification fingerprints only to balance outputs within each sublane. Cap every retry count and fill rare shortfalls with fresh unconstrained tower tuples, never catalogue polynomials.
hypotheses.label: Constrained nested quadratic towers
hypotheses.mission: Attack entirely missing groups, especially small imprimitive groups plausibly arising from non-generic three-level 2-extension actions.
hypotheses.rationale: Generation 3 established this mechanism as real but sparse: it found two missing pairs and nine fresh pair hits. The next useful experiment is therefore a tightly capped, better-stratified tower search rather than scaling the old sampler indiscriminately. Norm classes of b0+b1u and of the final radicand control which sign automorphisms extend through the tower, providing algebraic subgroup variation rather than cosmetic coefficient variation.

hypotheses.expected_result: Fresh missing signatures—principally r=4 or r=8—in groups that already have another signature, with broader group reach than the failed chamber-only experiment. The negative-d lane should also provide controlled r=2 and r=6 probes where the quartic base has one or three real roots.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Measure against the matched unconditioned trace-cover control on identical seeds. Falsify the idea if joint conditioning yields no fresh missing signature and no increase in fresh pair hits, or if almost all selected square-class strata collapse to the same verified group-signature outcomes.
hypotheses.hypothesis: For P(x)=x⁴g(x+s+d/x), the group geometry comes from a quartic base together with four quadratic fibers, while the real signature is controlled explicitly by the locations of the real roots of g relative to the branch thresholds. When d=e²>0, each base root outside [-2e-s,2e-s] contributes two real roots; for d<0, every real base root contributes two. Simultaneously stratifying the square classes of g(-s+2e), g(-s-2e), and disc(g) changes relations among the four fiber discriminants. Joint chamber and square-class selection should therefore reach missing r=4 and r=8 pairs that signature-only resampling missed.
hypotheses.implementation: Deterministically enumerate monic irreducible quartics g from generic, even, reciprocal, and cubic-resolvent-constrained parameterizations. Combine them with nonzero e, shifts s, and d drawn from both e² and -e², then expand x⁴g(x+s+d/x) exactly to a monic integral octic with constant term d⁴. Certify its real-root count using Sturm sequences and, for positive d, independently verify the count of base roots outside the two integer thresholds. Compute squarefree kernels of g(-s±2e) and disc(g), reduced to valuation/sign fingerprints rather than expensive full factorization. Select within requested signature strata 0,2,4,6,8 only when the candidate also adds a rare square-class or good-prime factorization fingerprint; transfer unused quota to the rarest compatible joint stratum. Keep a matched unconditioned trace-cover control quota so the effect of conditioning is measurable.
hypotheses.label: Square-class-aware trace-cover chambers
hypotheses.mission: Attack missing signatures inside partially covered groups without repeating signature conditioning as a stand-alone strategy.
hypotheses.rationale: The earlier signature-conditioned candidate produced no gain because it mostly moved outputs between real-root chambers already occupied by the same algebraic kernels. This version makes signature only one coordinate: candidates must also diversify branch-value square classes, quartic factor patterns, and ramification fingerprints. The construction retains an exact reason for both its block action and its real-root count.

hypotheses.expected_result: Lower raw volume than the incumbent but access to at least one primitive group or pair absent from all block-based lanes. Even without a new pair, verified octics exhibiting local cycle fingerprints unattainable by the imprimitive families would justify a larger benchmark.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Falsify the focused construction if it produces essentially no irreducible verified octics at screening scale, if its verified outputs all duplicate already-covered pair behavior without distinctive primitive-compatible local cycles, or if bounded modular norm computation cannot meet the slot runtime.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The eight nonzero points of E[3] form a natural transitive degree-eight orbit under a generic mod-3 Galois image. Orbit polynomials of theta(P)=y(P)+k x(P) therefore access primitive GL(2,3)-type actions that binary towers, reciprocal lifts, and ordinary compositions structurally cannot produce. Carefully chosen integral models and local curve conditions should turn the previously under-tested 3-torsion idea into a viable source of missing primitive groups or signatures.
hypotheses.implementation: Enumerate short Weierstrass curves E:y²=x³+Ax+B with A=3a, nonzero curve discriminant, and deterministic small-to-medium shells. Then psi3(x)/3=x⁴+2A*x²+4B*x-A²/3 is monic integral. In the quartic algebra defined by psi3/3, form the multiplication matrix X and compute the polynomial norm det((T-kX)²-(X³+A*X+B*I)); its coefficients give a monic integral degree-eight polynomial whose roots are y(P)+k x(P) for the eight nonzero 3-torsion points. Use a fraction-free polynomial determinant or modular reconstruction, not a symbolic resultant. Vary nonzero k and quadratic-twist/CM versus non-CM curve strata, but deduplicate fields heuristically using discriminant and local patterns so changes of primitive element do not consume the budget. Preselect curves using Frobenius traces modulo several good primes, translating each trace into the induced cycle fingerprint on the eight nonzero vectors. Apply the rational-factor sieve and bounded retries before emitting vectors.
hypotheses.label: Elliptic 3-torsion orbit octics
hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different primitive algebraic construction rather than another quadratic block system.
hypotheses.rationale: Both earlier primitive-action proposals were pruned before meaningful benchmark evidence, so their construction has not been falsified. Focusing on one explicit orbit, avoiding symbolic algebra, and selecting curves through cheap local 3-torsion fingerprints addresses the prior low screening yield while preserving the genuinely new action.

hypotheses.expected_result: No timeouts, verification near the incumbent’s current 0.892 fraction, and discovery performance close to or above its six fresh missing pairs and 67 fresh pair hits, with evidence showing which lanes are actually necessary. The protected tower share should add occasional missing-group hits without destabilizing seed-wide coverage.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Reject the adaptive replacement if it times out, falls below 0.85 verified fraction, loses more than 20 percent of incumbent fresh-pair hits on matched seeds, or assigns tower capacity repeatedly without any marginal pair hit after deduplication against the four incumbent lanes.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The incumbent’s success comes from complementary structural lanes and fingerprint selection, but fixed 30/30/25/15 quotas need not match each seed’s supply of irreducible, locally novel candidates. A small deterministic pilot followed by marginal-novelty quota allocation can retain the six-pair, all-seed robustness with fewer redundant candidates. The recovered capacity can support a protected, tightly capped nested-tower lane without repeating the timeout-prone oversized-pool implementations.
hypotheses.implementation: Retain the reciprocal trace, non-autonomous quadratic tree, square-discriminant critical-value, and Eisenstein control geometries, but give each branch-preserving deformations: variable reciprocal fiber d; affine constants at every tree level; two denominator-safe cubic q templates for f'=8xq²; and several Eisenstein primes. Add the tower engine from A only as a protected 5–10 percent lane. First generate a pilot of at most max(12,ceil(budget/40)) candidates per lane and record sieve survival, unique root-count/factor-pattern/valuation cells, and generation cost. Allocate remaining slots by deterministic diminishing returns—the next slot goes to the lane with the largest number of new fingerprint cells per attempted candidate—subject to minimum and maximum shares. Limit the complete preselection pool to at most 3*budget+O(1), use modular discriminant valuations during selection, and compute exact integer discriminants only for finalists and a small low-height reserve. Perform global canonical deduplication and round-robin emission across selected lanes.
hypotheses.label: Bounded adaptive incumbent ablation
hypotheses.mission: Exploit and improve the useful incumbent mechanisms while directly addressing redundancy and timeout risk.
hypotheses.rationale: Generation 3’s strongest evidence favors the four-lane portfolio, while the critic explicitly requests family ablation and admits towers only when they add post-deduplication yield. Previous incumbent-improvement implementations failed operationally, so strict linear pool bounds and cheap fingerprints are part of the mathematical hypothesis, not incidental engineering.

hypotheses.expected_result: Broad fresh-seed reach comparable to the incumbent, additional missing pairs contributed by more than one construction, and occasional improvements among the listed large-discriminant records from the low-height reserve. Family attribution should reveal whether novelty comes from rare small clusters rather than merely extreme maximin points.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Compare set-cover, exploration, and record-reserve selections separately. Falsify the portfolio thesis if the combined archive produces no missing pair beyond its best single family, loses substantial seed reach relative to the incumbent, or spends its record reserve without either a field-discriminant improvement or demonstrably distinct verified fingerprints.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Greedy maximin distance can overvalue extreme but repetitive fingerprints, while fixed round-robin can miss small rare clusters. A deterministic novelty archive combining coverage, protected exploration, and a subordinate low-height Pareto reserve should sample more distinct algebraic neighborhoods. Pooling several genuinely different constructions before selection can discover missing pairs that no single lane reaches reliably and can naturally expose smaller-discriminant representatives of already-solved difficult pairs.
hypotheses.implementation: Build bounded pools from five sources: generalized reciprocal trace covers, non-autonomous quadratic trees, constrained nested towers, elliptic 3-torsion norms, and sparse low-height Eisenstein octics. Give every candidate a fingerprint containing exact real-root count; factor degrees at a seed-rotated set of 6–8 small good primes; truncated discriminant valuations; polynomial-discriminant square class; construction stratum; and coarse height/sparsity bins. Fill 70 percent of the budget by greedy set-cover gain over individual fingerprint features and feature pairs, 20 percent by deterministic hash-ranked sampling from underrepresented construction strata, and 10 percent by a Pareto order on polynomial discriminant, coefficient height, and Mahler-style root bound. If any novelty candidate competes for space, evict record-reserve candidates first. Rotate the auxiliary primes and family enumeration order from the public seed, but use no hidden state or catalogue outcomes. Bound total pool size by 4*budget+constant, cache finite-field factorizations, globally canonicalize x↦-x equivalents, and use deterministic Eisenstein completion only for exact-budget shortfalls.
hypotheses.label: Novelty archive with record reserve
hypotheses.mission: Run a complementary global exploration portfolio that prioritizes new local behavior while preserving a small route to difficult discriminant improvements.
hypotheses.rationale: The winning generation showed that local factorization and ramification data are effective catalogue-free surrogates, and also produced the only discriminant improvement. This proposal preserves that principle but changes the selection algorithm and broadens its sources. Record optimization remains subordinate: a candidate with a previously unseen local cell always outranks a merely smaller discriminant proxy.

details.thesis: Preserve the incumbent’s demonstrated local-fingerprint diversity as a benchmark, but spend this generation on orthogonal sources of group geometry rather than additional coefficient perturbations. The five implementations respectively probe nested 2-extension actions, signature-controlled trace covers, primitive 3-torsion actions, a bounded adaptive repair of the incumbent, and a global exploration/record portfolio. Every generator must derive all parameters deterministically from seed and position, reject reducible or duplicate outputs with bounded work, and use catalogue labels only for post-evaluation analysis—not during generation or selection.

avoid: Treating higher raw benchmark scores for D or E as evidence that they outperformed A on the stated discovery objective.
Claiming B or C failed algebraically when both were pruned before benchmark evaluation.
Using S as evidence for or against its portfolio hypothesis; the solver process failed.
Repeating the previous generation’s E-centered diagnosis or its incompatible metrics.
Inferring any hidden seed or group-signature identities from aggregate counts.
Scaling A indiscriminately without measuring verification rate, runtime, and marginal novelty after deduplication.
feedback.diagnosis: A is the clear discovery winner in the supplied generation: its nested quadratic towers produced 4 fresh missing pairs, 83 fresh pair hits, and coverage on 56 fresh seeds. This validates the hypothesis that genuinely nested towers access useful degree-eight actions missed by the existing reciprocal, Cartesian, and preimage-tree families. D and E each found only 1 fresh pair on 1 seed, so their higher numeric benchmark scores did not translate into comparable discovery breadth. D’s adaptive allocation did achieve 3 discriminant improvements, making it useful for record refinement but not as the lead discovery strategy. B and C were pruned at screening and therefore provide no benchmark evidence; C remains untested rather than disproved. S failed operationally and yielded no measurements. The previous feedback describes a different result set and must not be reused: in this generation A—not E—won, with 4/83/56 and no discriminant improvements.
feedback.next_generation_direction: Make A’s nested-tower construction the primary lane and run a deterministic parameter-family ablation: separately benchmark generic, norm-square, and conjugate-pair constraints under equal runtime caps, recording verified yield, marginal missing-pair hits after deduplication, seed reach, and cost per verified polynomial. Concentrate the next full budget on the best complementary mixture, while reserving a small fixed D-style lane solely for low-discriminant improvements.
what_worked: A’s genuinely nested quadratic towers delivered broad, seed-robust novelty: 4 missing pairs, 83 pair hits, and 56 seed hits.
Alternating generic and constrained tower parameters appears to sample multiple useful transitive actions rather than a single narrow family.
D’s pilot-based allocation found 3 discriminant improvements, showing value as a small secondary record-search lane.

hypotheses.expected_result: At least one constrained lane should repeatedly realize one or more entirely absent transitive groups, while the generic reserve preserves high verification and broad fresh-seed reach. The solver should match or beat the incumbent runtime per verified octic rather than gaining novelty through more retries.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Under equal wall-clock caps, compare each lane and the combined scheduler on verified fraction, marginal missing-pair hits after cross-lane deduplication, fresh-seed reach, and milliseconds per verified polynomial. Falsify the claim if no constrained lane adds an entirely missing group beyond the generic lane, or if the mixture's gain disappears after equalizing runtime.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The four-way tower mixture obscures which algebraic constraints caused generation 4's broad novelty. Generic towers, square relative-norm towers, base-times-square norm towers, and conjugate-pair final radicands impose different index conditions on the binary-tree Galois action. A runtime-balanced ablation with protected generic capacity will concentrate outputs in the one or two constrained actions responsible for entirely missing groups while retaining the seed robustness of unconstrained towers.
hypotheses.implementation: Keep the exact 8-dimensional tower arithmetic and characteristic-polynomial construction, but rewrite the scheduler as three principal lanes: 50% generic radicands, 25% parametrized square/base-square relative norms, and 25% conjugate-pair or trace-zero final radicands. Within each lane enumerate small parameters by deterministic expanding L1 shells, vary the primitive element over several sparse coefficient masks, and cap arithmetic work per accepted candidate. Record lane-local attempts internally and transfer a starved slot first to the least-used principal lane, then to a fresh generic tower. Require a nonzero constant, monicity, canonical uniqueness, and finite-field factor patterns whose subset-sum intersection rules out every proper rational factor. Remove the current ad hoc fourth-way round robin and its weak unconstrained fallback loop. Return exactly budget vectors.
hypotheses.label: Nested-tower subgroup ablation
hypotheses.mission: Attack entirely missing groups, prioritizing 8T5, 8T12, 8T25, 8T33, 8T34, 8T36, 8T37, 8T43, and 8T48 without encoding their identities in the solver.
hypotheses.rationale: Nested towers are the only measured mechanism in the immediately preceding generation with substantial discovery breadth: 4 fresh missing pairs, 83 fresh hits, and hits on 56 seeds. The critic specifically calls for separate measurement of generic, norm-square, and conjugate-pair constraints and warns against indiscriminate scaling. Equal output counts are misleading because constrained lanes have different rejection costs, so allocation should be by generation work rather than raw attempted tuples.

hypotheses.expected_result: The generated set should have sharply higher realized proportions of r=8 and r=4 than the incumbent while retaining several reciprocal-lift Galois actions already observed at other signatures. Success means new signatures within partially covered groups, even if it discovers fewer distinct groups than A.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Measure requested-versus-verified signature accuracy, verification rate, and fresh missing signatures against an equal-runtime unconditioned reciprocal baseline. Falsify if chamber certification does not materially raise useful r=8/r=4 pair hits, or if all added outputs remain confined to already complete groups.
hypotheses.hypothesis: For P(x)=x^4 g(x+s+d/x), the transitive action is supplied by a quartic base with coupled quadratic fibers, but its signature can be selected before expansion. If d=q^2>0, each real root y of g outside [s-2q,s+2q] contributes two real roots of P; roots inside contribute none. If d<0, every real root of g contributes two. Constructing irreducible quartics in certified root chambers should move mass among r=0, r=4, and r=8 without changing the structural family, exposing signatures that coefficient-randomized reciprocal lifts rarely visit.
hypotheses.implementation: Generate monic quartics as g(y)=product(y-m_i)-epsilon using distinct deterministic integer centers, small nonzero epsilon, and also two-real-root and zero-real-root analogues. Certify the quartic root count and the placement of roots relative to s±2q using exact Sturm signs before forming P. Interleave target cells r=8, r=4, and r=0 in proportions 50/30/20; use d<0 sparingly as a second geometry. Expand the Laurent expression exactly to ascending integral coefficients, reject zero constants and canonical duplicates, and apply the existing cheap good-prime subset-sum irreducibility certificate. Enumerate centers and epsilon by small shells and bounded retries. Delete generic quartic generation that cannot certify its chamber, since it consumes runtime without serving this mission.
hypotheses.label: Certified signature chambers
hypotheses.mission: Attack missing signatures in partially covered groups, especially the many absent r=8 cases and the r=4 or r=6 gaps in 8T17, 8T19, 8T30, 8T32, 8T38, 8T40, 8T42, and 8T49.
hypotheses.rationale: The earlier signature-conditioned lift reached a screening score near 22100 but was pruned, so it was not algebraically falsified. The current catalogue shows that missing signatures, particularly total reality, are a major remaining source of pairs. Exact chamber construction is stronger than post hoc Sturm rejection because nearly every expanded octic is aimed at the requested signature.

hypotheses.expected_result: The generic and constrained relative extensions should contribute transitive groups with local cycle fingerprints not produced by A or B, with a verified fraction high enough to survive screening. A fresh entirely missing group is the principal success criterion.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Compare against equal-runtime Cartesian quartic/quadratic composita and generic nested towers. Falsify if the relative construction supplies no new group or pair after deduplication, if its fingerprints are almost entirely contained in the baselines, or if matrix construction makes cost per verified output more than roughly three times the incumbent without rare discoveries.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Let alpha generate a quartic field and adjoin w with w^2=q(alpha). The eight conjugates pair quadratic fibers whose radicands depend on the quartic embedding, unlike a Cartesian compositum with one rational quadratic field. Generic q produces a C2-wreath-S4-type action, while square-norm and conjugate-product constraints cut out distinct transitive subactions. Characteristic polynomials of theta=w+t(alpha) should therefore reach degree-eight groups missed by independent fibers and three-step binary towers.
hypotheses.implementation: Generate irreducible monic quartics f for several base geometries, then represent Q(alpha,w) in the basis 1,alpha,alpha^2,alpha^3,w,alpha*w,alpha^2*w,alpha^3*w with reductions f(alpha)=0 and w^2=q(alpha). Compute the 8x8 multiplication matrix of theta=w+t0+t1*alpha+t2*alpha^2 and its monic characteristic polynomial by fraction-free Faddeev-LeVerrier or Bareiss elimination. Use three protected lanes: generic linear/quadratic q; q with resultant Res(f,q) parametrized as a square; and difference-of-squares q=u(alpha)^2-d*v(alpha)^2. Reject collapsed extensions, zero constants, duplicates, and candidates not certified irreducible by several good-prime factor patterns. Use expanding low-height shells and a fixed operation cap; remove all E[3] division-polynomial machinery.
hypotheses.label: Quadratic extensions of quartic fields
hypotheses.mission: Introduce a genuinely different structured construction aimed at degree-eight actions absent from binary towers and Cartesian quartic-by-quadratic products.
hypotheses.rationale: The previous elliptic 3-torsion construction screened very poorly and should be replaced rather than accumulated. A quartic-relative quadratic extension retains a genuinely new action but needs only small exact integer matrices, making it far cheaper and less fragile. It also supplies direct algebraic constraints on the fiber-sign subgroup without catalogue knowledge.

hypotheses.expected_result: Discovery should approach the robust generation-3 portfolio with substantially lower candidate-generation time, while the low-height ordering and discriminant tie-break produce occasional improvements among high-record pairs such as 8T15|8, 8T49|0, or 8T29|8 without hard-coding those targets.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Benchmark against the original fixed-quota portfolio at equal wall time. Falsify if fresh missing-pair count or seed reach drops materially, if discriminant improvements vanish across fresh seeds, or if exact discriminant ranking dominates runtime without producing either novelty or records.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The accepted generation-3 portfolio found six missing pairs across every fresh seed, but its later adaptive variant mostly improved discriminants and found only one fresh pair. The useful ingredient was complementary algebraic geometry, not a large maximin pool. Streaming low-height enumeration with protected family quotas, exact early rejection, and within-fingerprint preference for small polynomial discriminant should preserve discovery coverage at lower runtime and naturally find smaller-discriminant fields.
hypotheses.implementation: Retain only four constructors: nonautonomous three-quadratic preimage trees, reciprocal trace lifts, integral square-discriminant critical-value octics, and low-height Eisenstein controls. Allocate 40/30/20/10 slots with no pilot-driven quota takeover. For each slot stream at most a small constant number of shell-ordered candidates, perform cheap modular squarefreeness and rational-factor subset-sum tests first, and compute the exact polynomial discriminant only for survivors. Maintain small buckets keyed by construction, exact real-root count, and good-prime factor degrees; within an overfull bucket choose the lower discriminant proxy, but never evict a candidate from a previously empty bucket. Avoid affine translates of the same field and eliminate the old oversized maximin candidate pool. Fill deficits from fresh preimage trees, then deterministic Eisenstein octics, preserving exact uniqueness and budget.
hypotheses.label: Lean incumbent refinement
hypotheses.mission: Exploit useful incumbent reciprocal, preimage-tree, square-discriminant, and Eisenstein mechanisms while improving their discovery efficiency and preserving a small discriminant-record lane.
hypotheses.rationale: D's generation-4 pilot allocation produced three discriminant improvements but only one fresh pair on one seed, so adaptive allocation should remain subordinate. The current source also carries substantial superseded machinery. A coherent, smaller implementation can revisit proven families without copying their expensive global selection logic.

hypotheses.expected_result: The portfolio should retain much of A's discovery rate while reaching complementary C- and B-type actions on more fresh seeds, with lower runtime and lower seed-to-seed variance than pool-based novelty selection. The small final reserve may also improve difficult field-discriminant records.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Compare fresh pairs, marginal pair hits, seed reach, runtime, and between-seed variance with both pure A and the rejected generation-4 novelty archive. Falsify if it finds no pair beyond pure A, if protected cells reduce A's discoveries without compensation, or if low-discrepancy scheduling is indistinguishable from ordinary round robin across the fresh-seed panel.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Pseudorandom shell schedules can repeatedly sample nearby parameter regions even when several algebraic families are present. A deterministic low-discrepancy design over family, constraint type, signature request, coefficient scale, and local congruence cell should cover the product space more uniformly without generating a huge pool. Interleaving virtual substreams derived publicly from the input seed should improve robustness while explicit protected cells prevent common fingerprints from consuming the budget.
hypotheses.implementation: Map candidate indices through a scrambled Halton or bit-reversal sequence whose scramble is a documented mix of the supplied seed and public lane constants. Use coordinates to choose among nested towers (45%), relative quartic extensions (20%), certified reciprocal chambers (15%), preimage trees (15%), and low-height Eisenstein/critical controls (5%); within each family choose constraint subtype, sign chamber, shell, sparse primitive-element mask, and residue conditions. Generate online with at most two candidates of overproduction per output, using occupancy caps on coarse cells (family, signature, first two usable prime patterns) rather than pairwise maximin distance. Every coarse cell receives a protected initial slot before caps relax. In the final 8% of slots, prefer the smallest polynomial-discriminant survivor within already represented cells, so record refinement cannot displace new structural coverage. Canonicalize, deduplicate, and use fresh generic tower or Eisenstein completions to return exactly budget vectors.
hypotheses.label: Low-discrepancy exploration portfolio
hypotheses.mission: Design a complementary cross-family exploration strategy that reduces seed variance, protects rare algebraic cells, and reserves limited capacity for difficult discriminant records.
hypotheses.rationale: Generation 4 showed that higher aggregate scores for D and E did not imply discovery breadth, and the greedy novelty archive regressed to one fresh pair. This mission therefore avoids another maximin selector. It treats coverage as an experimental design problem, retains towers as the evidence-backed anchor, and gives discriminant search only a small lexicographically subordinate reserve.

details.thesis: Treat discovery breadth, signature control, algebraic action, incumbent refinement, and portfolio robustness as separate experimental questions. The strongest evidence is the generation-4 nested-tower result (4 fresh pairs, 83 hits, 56 seeds), so one mission performs the requested ablation rather than indiscriminately enlarging it. The other missions pursue different mechanisms: explicit real-root chambers, quartic-relative quadratic extensions, lean refinement of proven portfolio families, and low-discrepancy cross-family exploration. Every solver must stream deterministic constructions, reject duplicates canonically, use bounded retries, and fill any deficit with fresh generic constructions rather than catalogue data or fixed answer polynomials.
